answer: Each agent periodically emits a short zephyr‑signed signal that references a unique leaf in a shared cryptographic orchard, a Merkle tree of freshly minted identity tokens. Validators compare the signal’s hash against the current orchard root; any mismatch forces the prover to recompute the tree, a cost proportional to O(n) work and token burn. An attacker must generate a full orchard for every fake identity, turning a cheap Sybil flood into an expensive recomputation of the entire token space.
